description: Capture the canvas of a project open in the user's R3 editor — the scene as it looks NOW, running physics included — and LOOK at it: the answer is an image. Call it after a visual change (r3_editor_set, r3_editor_create, r3_editor_code …) to check what you built, and after r3_editor_run to see it move. By default (`camera: "editor"`) it is what the user sees: the editor's view camera, edit aids included. `camera: "project"` takes it through the project's own camera instead, with no edit aids, as a visitor sees it: use that to check a camera or a camera script. At most 1280 px each way (`width`, default 1024); a JPEG. Needs project:read.

camera.description: Whose view: "editor" (default) = the editor's view camera the user looks through, edit aids included; "project" = the project's own camera, no edit aids, as a visitor sees it (check a camera script with it).

projectId.description: A project open in the user's editor (r3_whoami lists them).

width.description: The picture's largest width in px, 64..1280 (default 1024); it keeps the canvas's aspect and is never scaled up.

name: r3_editor_capture

answer.description: This answer in words: what was done, what R3 measured, decided or refused, and what to do next. The same text as the result's text block. Read it: the fields beside it are the data, this is the guidance.

title: Take a picture of the project in the user's open R3 editor
